app.name: Pipedrive Marketplace app (own OAuth app for Composio)

verdict.summary: Creating and testing your own Pipedrive OAuth app is quick and self-serve, and Composio has no managed Pipedrive app, so you must supply your own client_id and client_secret. Review only applies if you distribute through the Marketplace as a public app; private apps shared by installation link skip Marketplace approval.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 2-4 hours for the app, Composio connection and private-app setup; 1-2 days more to prepare Marketplace listing, compliance pages, demo video and test accounts for a public app
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30-60 minutes after you have a developer sandbox account
verdict.approval_wait: None for private apps or your own account; up to 21 business days for public Marketplace app review (provider-stated)

gates.name: Draft app, your own account
gates.unlocks: You create the app in Developer Hub, install it into your sandbox company and connect your own Pipedrive account through Composio.
limits: A draft app can only be authorized by users in the same Pipedrive company account where the app was created (community-reported, consistent with Pipedrive FAQ).
Access tokens expire after 60 minutes; refresh tokens expire after 60 days of non-use.
gates.time_to_reach: Under 1 hour once a developer sandbox account exists

gates.name: Invited or test users (private app installation link)
gates.unlocks: A private app can be installed by other Pipedrive companies through a direct installation link, without Marketplace approval. Choose this at app creation: app type cannot be changed later.
limits: App type (public or private) is fixed at creation and cannot be changed later.
No install cap or user-count limit was found in the research; treat as unknown.
Installing an admin-scoped app requires an account admin.
gates.time_to_reach: Same session as Gate 1 if you choose a private app; no review wait

gates.name: Anyone via Pipedrive Marketplace (public app)
gates.unlocks: Public, listed Marketplace app that any Pipedrive company can discover and install.
limits: Requires Marketplace listing content, Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, pricing page link, install instructions and support contact before submission.
Requires a demo video covering each scope and fully working test accounts for the review team.
Approved apps stay unlisted until you click Publish in Developer Hub.
Pipedrive decides approval in its sole discretion and the decision is final.
gates.time_to_reach: Up to 21 business days of review after submission, plus your preparation time (provider-stated)

steps.title: Get a Pipedrive developer sandbox account
steps.detail: App creation requires a developer sandbox account. If you do not have one, sign up through the Pipedrive developer site. Whether signup is free and instant was not verified.
gotchas: Do not rely on a guessed OAuth docs path on developers.pipedrive.com; one probe returned 404.

steps.title: Open Developer Hub
steps.detail: Log in to your sandbox company. Open Settings from the top-right profile menu, then use the company name drop-down to reach the Developer Hub.

steps.title: Create the app and choose its type
steps.detail: Create a new app. Choose public (OAuth 2.0, Marketplace-listed, needs approval for listing) or private (shared by installation link, no Marketplace approval). This choice cannot be changed later. If you only need your own company or a few named companies, choose private.

values.label: App type
values.value: Private for installation-link distribution without review; Public for Marketplace listing

gotchas: Community reports say a public app that was never approved can be returned to draft and need a new review cycle if converted.

steps.title: Fill Basic info and set the callback URL
steps.detail: In Basic info, enter an App name and paste the callback URL into the OAuth Callback URL field. This is the OAuth redirect_uri and only one callback URL is allowed per app. A placeholder can be saved at creation, but it must be replaced with a working URL before any review submission.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Whether Composio's default callback must be registered in your own app was not confirmed. Verify against Composio's current docs before relying on it.
Composio's record lists a v1 auth-apps path while the probe used a v3 callback path; check the production value.

steps.title: Select only the scopes you need
steps.detail: Open the OAuth & access scopes tab and select scopes. Composio's default is six broad full-access scopes, so do not copy them blindly. The base scope is always on. Users accept or deny all requested scopes together.

values.label: Composio default scopes
values.value: contacts:full, leads:full, mail:full, activities:full, products:full, projects:full

gotchas: Admin scope lets the app manage pipelines, stages, fields, users and webhooks. Installers must be account admins, and non-admin installs can break admin-level calls unless the app handles them.
Changes to scopes may force re-approval after the app is listed.

steps.title: Copy client_id and client_secret into Composio
steps.detail: After saving Basic info, the client_id and client_secret appear in the OAuth & access scopes tab. Enter them in your Composio Pipedrive OAuth2 auth config. Composio has no managed Pipedrive app, so this step is required. Pipedrive exchanges codes using HTTP Basic auth with these credentials.
gotchas: Client secret rotation and storage guidance were not fetched; store the secret server-side only.

steps.title: Install and test in the sandbox company
steps.detail: Use Install & test to install the draft app into the sandbox company, then run an authorization through Composio with your own account. Confirm install, uninstall, reconnect, and that access tokens refresh after 60 minutes. Agent can script the token-refresh check against the Pipedrive API.
gotchas: Refresh tokens expire after 60 days of non-use; an expired one forces the user to reinstall and reauthorize.
Do not store personal API tokens; reviewers check this.

steps.title: Choose a distribution path for invited users
steps.detail: For invited companies on a private app, share the installation link from Developer Hub. No Marketplace approval is needed for private apps. Note that a third-party source says an app sold to customers needs Pipedrive approval even if never listed; confirm with Pipedrive before selling a private app commercially.
gotchas: Private apps cannot be published in the Marketplace.
No install cap was found; confirm limits with Pipedrive for larger rollouts.

steps.title: Prepare Marketplace listing content
steps.detail: For a public app, fill in general info: built-by company name, app category, a short summary, a full description, an app icon, and 1 to 5 listing images. Preview the listing in Developer Hub before submitting.
gotchas: Common first-review failures include minimal landing-page effort, missing required fields, and unclear app purpose.

steps.title: Draft compliance pages and install instructions
steps.detail: An agent can draft the Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, step-by-step installation instructions and per-scope justification text. You must publish the pages on live URLs, add a pricing page link, and supply a support contact.
gotchas: The approval checklist requires all of these before submission.

steps.title: Record the demo video and set up test accounts
steps.detail: Record a demo video explaining the use of each permission and scope. Create fully working, up-to-date test accounts for the Pipedrive review team and keep a contact available during review. Recording the video and creating accounts require your identity and access, so agents cannot do them.
gotchas: Keep test accounts working through the review window.

steps.title: Agree to the Developer Partner Agreement
steps.detail: Accept the Pipedrive Developer Partner Agreement in Developer Hub. This is required before the app can be sent to review. Pipedrive decides approval in its sole discretion and the decision is final.
gotchas: Pipedrive can also remove apps from the Marketplace at its discretion.

steps.title: Submit for review and confirm the contact email
steps.detail: Enter the test account details in the submission flow and submit. Confirm the email sent to the main contact address; the app moves to review and shows 'In review' status. Required fields are validated at submission, so replace the placeholder callback URL first.
gotchas: Submission is blocked until the contact email is confirmed.

steps.title: Wait for the review decision
steps.detail: Pipedrive says public app reviews may take up to 21 business days. Approval sends an email and updates the Developer Hub status. Rejection emails state the reasons, and you cannot resubmit until they are resolved.
gotchas: Reviewers check install and uninstall, token refresh at 60 minutes, not storing personal tokens, rate limits, and extensions loading without errors (community-reported).

steps.title: Publish the approved app
steps.detail: After approval, an approved public app stays unlisted until you open the app menu in Developer Hub and click Publish.

requirements.detail: Required to create apps in Developer Hub. Signup cost and speed were not verified.

requirements.item: App name and OAuth Callback URL
requirements.detail: The two required Basic info fields. Callback is the redirect_uri; one callback URL per app. Placeholder allowed at creation only.
Set in the OAuth & access scopes tab. client_id and client_secret appear in the same tab.
Lets other Pipedrive companies install without Marketplace approval. App type cannot be changed later.
Built-by company name, category, summary max 150 characters, full description, icon min 256x256 1:1, 1-5 images 16:10.

requirements.item: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, pricing page link, install instructions, support contact
requirements.detail: Required before submitting a public app.

requirements.item: Demo video and working test accounts
requirements.detail: Video must explain each permission and scope. Test accounts must be fully working and up to date for the review team.
Must be agreed in Developer Hub before submission.
Main contact email must be confirmed before the app moves to In review.

scopes.effect: Always enabled for every app; you do not select it.

scopes.scope: contacts:full, leads:full, mail:full, activities:full, products:full, projects:full (Composio defaults)
scopes.effect: Full-access scopes. Pipedrive does not label sensitivity tiers. Request only what the app needs; reviewers check each scope in the demo video.
Lets the app manage pipelines, stages, fields, users and webhooks. Installers must be account admins; non-admin installers can break admin-level calls unless handled.

blockers.symptom: App cannot be published; Developer Hub says a public app without approval cannot be published.
blockers.cause: Public apps must be approved before they can be listed, and private apps cannot be published in the Marketplace at all.
blockers.fix: For a Marketplace listing, submit the public app for review. For invited-only distribution, use a private app and installation link instead.

blockers.symptom: Converting a never-approved public app returns it to draft and requires a new review cycle.
blockers.cause: Community-reported behavior when converting an unapproved public app.
blockers.fix: Decide app type before creating the app. If you may later need a listing, start public, but expect review either way.

blockers.symptom: Submission rejected or blocked because required fields are missing or the callback is a placeholder.
blockers.cause: Required fields are validated at review submission; a placeholder callback URL must be replaced first.
blockers.fix: Replace the placeholder callback URL with the Composio callback URL, complete all listing and compliance fields, then resubmit.

blockers.symptom: External users cannot authorize the app while it is in draft.
blockers.cause: Draft apps are only authorized by users in the same company account where the app was created.
blockers.fix: Test with your own sandbox account in Gate 1. For other users, use a private app installation link or wait until the public app is Live.

blockers.symptom: Admin-level calls fail for some installers.
blockers.cause: The admin scope requires an account admin to install; non-admin installs can break admin-level calls.
blockers.fix: Only request admin if necessary, and handle non-admin installs in your app.

blockers.symptom: Users are forced to reinstall and reauthorize.
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens expire after 60 days of non-use, and access tokens expire after 60 minutes.
blockers.fix: Refresh access tokens before expiry and on each use, and handle refresh failures by prompting reauthorization.

blockers.cause: Rejection emails state reasons, and the app cannot be resubmitted until reasons are resolved. Reviewers check the policy items on the checklist.
blockers.fix: Read the rejection email, fix each listed reason, then resubmit.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Pipedrive. Start with your own Pipedrive app and its client_id and client_secret, for both draft testing and any Marketplace path. Narrow Composio's six default '*:full' scopes to what you need. Confirm whether Composio's callback URL must be registered in your Pipedrive app before relying on it.

evidence.claim: Composio's toolkit record for Pipedrive lists no managed OAuth app and six default scopes: contacts:full, leads:full, mail:full, activities:full, products:full, projects:full.

Composio lists no managed OAuth app for Pipedrive; the OAuth2 config uses Composio's default scopes and Pipedrive's authorize and token endpoints, so a developer must supply their own Pipedrive app credentials.
Pipedrive's docs say developers create the app in the Developer Hub, which requires a developer sandbox account; the Developer Hub is reached from Settings via the company name drop-down.
Pipedrive says a developer sandbox account is needed for app creation and that you can sign up on the developer site if you lack one.
Pipedrive's developer site (developers.pipedrive.com) is where the sandbox account is requested; a direct probe of a guessed OAuth docs path on that site returned 404, so do not rely on that path.
Pipedrive offers two app types: public apps (OAuth 2.0, listed in the Marketplace) and private apps (API token or OAuth, shared via installation link). The app type cannot be changed later.
Pipedrive says OAuth 2.0 is mandatory for all public Marketplace apps and that, to access users' data, an app must be registered in the Marketplace where installation starts.

Private apps do not need Marketplace approval; they are shared with any Pipedrive company through a direct installation link. Pipedrive's approval page says submitting is unnecessary if the app is used internally only.
Third-party reporting says an app you sell to customers needs Pipedrive approval even if you never list it publicly.
Draft apps can only be authorized by users in the same Pipedrive account where the app was created; external users cannot authorize until the app is Live.
Pipedrive's developer FAQ says that a draft app's OAuth flow works for the correct company's account even while in draft mode.
Registration form for a public app: App name and OAuth Callback URL are the two required Basic info fields; the callback URL is the OAuth redirect_uri and only one callback URL is allowed per app.

Developer Hub notes a placeholder callback URL can be saved at creation, but it must be replaced with a working one before submitting for approval; the other required fields are validated at review submission.
Access scopes are required in the 'OAuth & access scopes' tab; the client_id and client_secret are shown in that same tab after saving Basic info.

Public-app registration requires general info: built-by company name, app category, a short summary (max 150 characters), a full description, an app icon (min 256x256, 1:1), and 1 to 5 listing images in 16:10 ratio.
Before submitting, the approval checklist requires a Terms of Service page, a Privacy Policy page, a link to a separate pricing page, step-by-step installation instructions, and a support contact.
Review requires a demo video explaining the use of each permission and scope, fully working up-to-date test accounts for the Pipedrive review team, and a contact available during review.
The submission flow asks for test account details, then requires a confirmed email to the main contact address before the app moves to review and shows 'In review' status.
Developer Hub says you must agree to the Pipedrive Developer Partner Agreement before the app can be sent to review.
Developer agreement: Pipedrive decides in its sole discretion whether to approve a Marketplace app, and that decision is final; Pipedrive can also remove apps from the Marketplace at its discretion.
Scopes are declared per app in the Developer Hub; the user accepts or denies all requested scopes together, so the docs advise requesting only what is necessary.

The 'base' scope is always enabled for every app; scopes listed include deals, mail, activities, contacts, products, leads, projects, webhooks, users (read), search, and admin, among others, each with read-only and full-access variants where applicable.

The 'admin' scope lets an app manage pipelines, stages, fields, users and webhooks; installing an admin-scoped app requires an account admin, and non-admin installers can break the app's admin-level calls unless the app handles them.

Pipedrive's docs do not label any scope as sensitive or restricted in the scopes page I read; the only review-relevant scope treatment is the admin-scope installation caveat and the requirement to justify each scope in the demo video.

Authorization starts by sending the user's browser to Pipedrive's OAuth authorize endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri and optional state; this step is only needed if you allow installation outside the Marketplace.

Authorization codes expire after 5 minutes. The code is exchanged at the token endpoint using HTTP Basic auth with client_id and client_secret; the Basic-auth form is preferred over putting credentials in the body.

Access tokens expire after 60 minutes (expires_in); refresh tokens expire if unused for 60 days, and each use resets that window. An expired refresh token forces the user to reinstall the app and go through authorization again.
Every access token is bound to the user who granted it, the company, the app, a set of scopes and an expiry; API calls go to the company-specific domain with a Bearer header.
Public-app approval timelines: Pipedrive states public app reviews may take up to 21 business days because of high demand and holidays.

Third-party reporting cites the same 21-business-day review window and lists reviewer checks: install and uninstall, token refresh at the 60-minute expiry, not storing personal API tokens, respecting rate limits, using v2 webhooks where possible, and extensions loading without errors.
Rejection emails state the reason; the app cannot be resubmitted until those reasons are resolved. Approval sends an email and the status changes in Developer Hub.
Pipedrive's developer documentation says an approved public app stays unlisted until the developer clicks Publish from the app's menu in Developer Hub.

Common first-review failures reported by Pipedrive's engineering team: minimal landing-page effort, missing required fields, and unclear app purpose. Pipedrive says the minimum-viable-product bar is often missed.
Pipedrive's checklist states apps must not collect or store a user's personal API token, must refresh tokens once the 60-minute lifetime expires, and must request only necessary scopes.
Pipedrive's Developer Hub FAQ says a public app without approval cannot be published, and a private app cannot be published in the Marketplace at all.
A community answer reports that converting a public app that was never approved can return it to draft and require a new review cycle before it can be published.
Pipedrive's app listing says changes to scopes, app name, and similar core settings may force re-approval; minor listing text and images can be updated in Developer Hub.
The app listing preview is available in Developer Hub before submitting, and the Developer Hub's 'Install & test' button installs the draft app into the sandbox company for testing.
Pipedrive's developer docs describe a 'Developer Hub' under Settings in the top-right profile menu; the hub is where apps, listings, and sandbox installs are managed.

open_questions: Whether Composio's default callback URI must be registered as the OAuth Callback URL in your own Pipedrive app, or whether your own callback is required. Verify against Composio's current docs before production.
Composio's record lists a v1 auth-apps path while the probe used a v3 callback path; check the production redirect value.
Whether developer sandbox signup is free and instant was not verified.
No install cap or rate limit specific to draft or unreviewed apps was found.
PKCE support is not stated in the pages read; treat as unknown.
Client secret rotation and credential handling were not read.
Pipedrive does not label scopes as sensitive or restricted; which scopes receive extra review scrutiny is unknown beyond the demo-video requirement.

Whether a private app can be sold to customers without Marketplace approval is unclear: Pipedrive's private-app page says it is shared by installation link, while a third-party source says sold apps need approval.
Reviewer rejection reasons beyond the general checklist were not captured in detail.
No OpenID Connect discovery was checked; Pipedrive's pages read do not mention OIDC.
